rv.q: "Rent" makes the musical theater joyously important again.
Now, the triumph is expected to repeat itself when 'Rent' reopens Monday on Broadway.
We still are crazy about the piece, and are delighted that it will be around for a long time.
Rent , it seems, has grown with age, rather than tarnished.
Still, due largely to Larson's way with words and musical notes, "Rent" builds a genuine emotional momentum.
The move to Broadway has magnified the show's flaws.

One positive exception to the waxworks impression is Annaleigh Ashford, whose blonde looks and flirtatious ways make for quite a different Maureen than the ferocious soul forged by the brunette Idina Menzel.
